blocks.html: WhatsApp OTP vs SMS OTP is not an either-or choice for most Indian businesses: SMS reaches every phone with network coverage, while WhatsApp is faster to complete and richer to use. The catch is that each channel has its own approval route, cost and failure points, and most teams only discover them after a login code goes missing.

This guide compares both channels on cost in INR, reach, compliance, security and user experience, for startups, SMBs and product teams across India. It then shows the setup most businesses should run: WhatsApp first, SMS as the safety net. Ojiva AI runs WhatsApp Business API and Bulk SMS on one platform. If you want both channels sized to your own login volumes, book a free demo.

sections.heading: WhatsApp OTP vs SMS OTP: The Short Answer

blocks.html: Use SMS OTP as your universal baseline and WhatsApp OTP as the faster, richer first attempt wherever your customers are on WhatsApp. For most Indian startups and SMBs, that means sending the OTP on WhatsApp first and falling back to SMS if the message is not delivered. Here is how the two compare at a glance.

items.title: Reach:
items.desc: WhatsApp OTP needs WhatsApp installed and a data connection. SMS OTP reaches any mobile number with network coverage.

items.title: Approval needed:
items.desc: WhatsApp uses a Meta-approved authentication template. SMS needs TRAI DLT: entity, sender ID, OTP template and Template ID.

items.title: Pricing basis:
items.desc: WhatsApp is billed at Meta's authentication rate, ₹0.1150 per delivered message in India, plus GST and provider fees. SMS is a per-message rate set by your provider.

items.title: User experience:
items.desc: WhatsApp offers a copy-code button, with one-tap autofill and zero-tap on Android. With SMS, the code arrives in the message and autofill depends on the device.

items.title: Message wording:
items.desc: WhatsApp authentication templates have a fixed body generated by Meta. SMS lets you write your own wording within the DLT-approved template.

items.title: Typical failure points:
items.desc: WhatsApp fails when the user has no WhatsApp, no data or an unapproved template. SMS fails on an unregistered header, a template mismatch or entity mapping errors.

sections.heading: How SMS OTP Works in India: DLT, Sender ID and Templates

blocks.html: Under TRAI's commercial communication regulations, every business sending commercial SMS in India registers on a DLT (Distributed Ledger Technology) platform, and OTP messages are included. If any link in the chain is missing, the message is blocked before it reaches the handset. Our step-by-step DLT guide covers the full process. Here is what matters for OTP.

items.title: Entity registration:
items.desc: your business is registered once as a Principal Entity with KYC documents and linked to your sending account.

items.title: Sender ID (header):
items.desc: a six-character header linked to your brand name, so users see a recognisable sender instead of an unknown number.

items.title: OTP template:
items.desc: registered under the transactional category, with your brand name in the text and a variable for the code. Each approved template gets a Template ID that must accompany every SMS.

items.title: Provider binding:
items.desc: your SMS provider must be linked to your entity, so every message can be traced back to you.

blocks.html: Most failed SMS OTPs trace back to configuration, not the network. An unapproved sender ID, a template whose text does not match the registered version, or a missing link between entity, header and template will all cause blocking. TRAI explains why registered delivery paths matter in its SMS traceability announcement.

SMS also has real strengths. It needs no app and no data connection, so it works on feature phones, in low-connectivity areas and for users who have never installed WhatsApp. That universal reach is why SMS OTP remains the default for many login and payment flows, and why it should stay in your flow even when WhatsApp is your first choice.

sections.heading: How WhatsApp OTP Works: Authentication Templates Explained

blocks.html: WhatsApp OTPs are sent as authentication template messages through the WhatsApp Business API. They are approved by Meta, not through DLT. DLT is a TRAI requirement for SMS only and does not apply to WhatsApp. Authentication templates are built for one purpose, which is delivering a verification code.

items.title: Fixed message body:
items.desc: Meta generates the text ("[code] is your verification code"), and only the code is a variable. The template cannot carry a header.

items.title: Optional safety lines:
items.desc: you can switch on a "do not share this code" security line and an expiry warning.

items.title: Copy code button:
items.desc: copies the OTP to the clipboard and works on all devices, including iPhone.

items.title: One-tap autofill:
items.desc: passes the code to your Android app when the user taps the button, for the smoothest experience.

items.title: Zero-tap:
items.desc: delivers the code to your Android app without the user leaving it. If WhatsApp's checks fail, or the user is not on Android, a one-tap or copy-code button is shown instead.

blocks.html: To start, you need an active WhatsApp Business API number through a provider, an approved authentication template and an API integration on your app or website. Collect a clear WhatsApp opt-in at sign-up, for example a checkbox that says "Send my OTP on WhatsApp". If you are still choosing between the app and the API, read WhatsApp vs WhatsApp Business vs WhatsApp Business API.

sections.heading: WhatsApp OTP vs SMS OTP Cost in India (INR)

blocks.html: Meta bills authentication messages per delivered message, based on the recipient's country. For Indian numbers, Meta's INR rate card lists ₹0.1150 per authentication message, and the rate did not change in the October 2026 revisions. Add 18% GST and your provider's fee. Volume discounts for authentication begin at 750,000 messages a month.
Worked example: 100,000 OTPs a month × ₹0.1150 = ₹11,500. GST at 18% adds ₹2,070, so Meta's charge comes to ₹13,570 before your provider's fees.

items.title: Compare cost per successful verification:
items.desc: Meta charges only for delivered authentication messages. With a WhatsApp-first flow you pay for SMS only on the share of users who need the fallback.

items.title: What SMS OTP costs:
items.desc: there is no single SMS OTP price in India. It depends on your provider, route and volume, so ask for an all-in per-OTP rate for a DLT-compliant route.

items.title: Authentication-international rate:
items.desc: if your WhatsApp Business Account is registered outside India and you send OTPs to Indian users, Meta can apply a separate rate of ₹2.4971 per message. Indian businesses sending from an India-registered account use the domestic rate. Confirm your setup with your provider.

items.title: Total cost of ownership:
items.desc: add GST, provider fees, retries and the engineering time spent on failed logins before declaring either channel cheaper.

sections.heading: Delivery, Reach and User Experience Compared

blocks.html: Cost is only half the story. The channel your users complete a login on fastest, and fail on least often, is the one that protects your sign-up and checkout conversion. Each channel covers the other's blind spot, which is the strongest argument for running both.

items.title: Reach across Indian users:
items.desc: WhatsApp OTP works only when the number has WhatsApp and the phone has data. SMS OTP needs neither, so feature-phone users and people in patchy coverage areas must stay on SMS.

items.title: Speed and login friction:
items.desc: copy-code and one-tap buttons cut the typing and app-switching that slow SMS OTP entry. On Android, one-tap and zero-tap can complete verification with almost no effort.

items.title: iPhone versus Android:
items.desc: one-tap and zero-tap work on Android only. iPhone users get the copy-code button, which is still faster than reading a code from another app.

items.title: Travellers and weak signal:
items.desc: SMS depends on cellular coverage and roaming can delay or block it. WhatsApp works over Wi-Fi, which helps users abroad or indoors with poor signal.

sections.heading: OTP Security and Compliance in India: TRAI, DLT, Meta and DPDP

blocks.html: Neither channel is secure on its own. OTP security comes from how you implement it, and compliance comes from following each channel's own rules. Keep the two tracks separate in your documentation, because SMS answers to TRAI and DLT while WhatsApp answers to Meta's template approval and opt-in policies.

items.title: Channel-specific risks:
items.desc: SMS OTP is exposed to SIM swap fraud and message interception. WhatsApp accounts can be targeted by social engineering, such as scammers asking users to forward a code. Meta's optional "do not share this code" line helps.

items.title: Rules that apply to both:
items.desc: keep codes short-lived and single-use, limit verification attempts, rate-limit resend requests and never write OTPs to application logs.

items.title: Resend discipline:
items.desc: show a resend cooldown instead of letting users request unlimited codes, which also controls your cost.

items.title: DPDP Act and consent:
items.desc: treat mobile numbers as personal data under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act. Collect them for a clear purpose, keep them only as long as needed, and capture a clear WhatsApp opt-in.

blocks.html: This is practical guidance rather than legal advice, so check your own obligations with a qualified professional.

sections.heading: Which Should You Use: WhatsApp OTP, SMS OTP or Both?

blocks.html: The right choice depends on who your users are and what a failed login costs you. Use the scenarios below as a starting point and adjust them to your own audience and traffic.

items.title: D2C and e-commerce sign-up or checkout:
items.desc: WhatsApp first for smartphone shoppers, with SMS fallback.

items.title: Android-heavy apps:
items.desc: WhatsApp one-tap or zero-tap for the smoothest login, with SMS fallback.

items.title: Fintech and NBFC onboarding:
items.desc: keep SMS as the guaranteed path, add WhatsApp for convenience, and check your regulator's and partners' requirements.

items.title: Feature-phone or low-data users:
items.desc: SMS OTP, because WhatsApp cannot reach them reliably.

items.title: Users who travel often:
items.desc: WhatsApp first over Wi-Fi, with SMS fallback.

sections.heading: How to Build a WhatsApp-First OTP Flow With SMS Fallback

blocks.html: A fallback flow gives you WhatsApp's speed without locking anyone out. It needs one rule: treat every code as single-use, so whichever channel the user completes verification on, earlier codes stop working.

items.title: Request:
items.desc: the user asks for an OTP on your login or checkout screen.

items.title: Send on WhatsApp:
items.desc: your system sends the code as a WhatsApp authentication template.

items.title: Track delivery:
items.desc: your application watches the delivery status through webhooks.

items.title: Fall back to SMS:
items.desc: if the message is not delivered within your timeout, send the code by SMS using your DLT-approved template.

items.title: Offer a manual switch:
items.desc: show a visible "Send via SMS" option so users can switch themselves.

blocks.alt: WhatsApp-first OTP flow with automatic SMS fallback for an Indian app

blocks.html: Avoid the common mistakes: sending the same OTP on both channels at once, which doubles cost and confuses users; launching without a fallback; going live before the SMS or WhatsApp template is approved; and using long expiry windows or unlimited resends. When plain SMS stops being enough for your other messages, the same contact list can move to richer channels, as our guide to upgrading bulk SMS to RCS explains.

items.q: Is WhatsApp OTP cheaper than SMS OTP in India?
items.a: It depends on your SMS provider's rates. Meta charges ₹0.1150 per delivered WhatsApp authentication message in India, plus 18% GST and your provider's fee. SMS OTP pricing varies by provider, route and volume. Compare the all-in cost per successful verification, including retries and fallbacks, instead of the per-message price alone.

items.q: Can WhatsApp replace SMS OTP completely?
items.a: For most businesses, not yet. WhatsApp OTP only reaches users who have WhatsApp on that number and an active data connection, while SMS works on any phone with network coverage. The safer approach is WhatsApp first for speed and user experience, with SMS OTP as an automatic fallback so no customer is locked out of signing in.

items.q: Do I need DLT registration for WhatsApp OTP?
items.a: No. DLT registration under TRAI's rules applies to SMS. WhatsApp OTPs are sent as authentication templates on the WhatsApp Business API, which are approved through Meta, and you must follow WhatsApp's opt-in policy. If you also send SMS OTP as a fallback, that SMS channel still needs your DLT entity, sender ID and approved template.

items.q: Why is my SMS OTP not delivered in India?
items.a: Common causes are configuration issues: an unapproved sender ID, message text that does not exactly match the registered DLT template, a missing link between your entity, header and template, or an SMS provider that is not bound to your entity. Check these first, then review your provider's delivery reports before suspecting the operator.

WhatsApp OTP can be as secure as SMS OTP when implemented well, but neither channel is secure on its own. Security comes from short expiry, single-use codes, attempt limits and resend cooldowns. Keep the optional "do not share this code" line that Meta offers in authentication templates to reduce social-engineering scams.

items.q: What is the difference between copy code, one-tap and zero-tap?
items.a: Copy code is a button that copies the OTP to the clipboard and works on all devices. One-tap autofill passes the code to your Android app when the user taps the button. Zero-tap delivers the code to your Android app without any tap, and falls back to a button if WhatsApp's checks fail or the user is not on Android.

items.q: What is the best OTP setup for Indian startups?
items.a: A WhatsApp-first flow with SMS fallback suits most startups. Send the OTP on WhatsApp, watch the delivery status, and trigger a DLT-approved SMS OTP if the message is not delivered within your timeout. Add a "send via SMS" option on the screen, enforce expiry and attempt limits, and run both channels through one provider for simpler reporting.
